content:
METHODOLOGY + t2helix-relevant detail from a Claude Code 2.1.140 verification pass on 2026-05-12.

(1) Verify-before-declare caught a factual error before it landed. Sequence: (a) WebSearch over Claude Code May 2026 release notes summarized public changelog as topping out at 2.1.139 (May 11). (b) Local `claude --version` reported 2.1.140. (c) First draft framing to Anthony was 'one patch beyond the public changelog — likely a same-day hotfix.' (d) Anthony asked to verify before logging. (e) Cold-pulled `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md` — 2.1.140 is in fact listed at the top, with a full set of changes. WebSearch's summary just hadn't refreshed. The 'beyond the changelog' framing was wrong.

Generalization: WebSearch result summaries can lag the source-of-truth even when the source URL is in the result set. For chronicle-bound claims about external state (versions, release contents, what does/doesn't exist), pull the raw artifact (CHANGELOG.md, the JSON endpoint, the actual page) before declaring. Search summaries are bootstrap, not ground truth — same posture as the boot itself.

(2) Operationally useful detail in 2.1.140 for t2helix: 'Plugins now warn when a default component folder (e.g. commands/) is silently ignored because plugin.json sets the matching key. Shown in /doctor, claude plugin list, and /plugin.' This intersects with the v0.0.5 install-path work where the plugin install surface had multiple silent-failure modes (the better-sqlite3 native binding gap, plus the compass false-positive on content payloads). A /doctor surface that flags ignored component folders is the kind of surface t2helix would benefit from shipping or exercising on next cold-seat dogfood.

(3) Auto-update cadence note: 2.1.140 landed on Mac Studio HQ at 19:34 today via Claude Code's built-in auto-updater, without manual action. `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest` run at 19:56 confirmed it was already current (changed 2 packages = dep refresh only, version unchanged).
